meta.sourceOfTruth: Product-owner transcript (authoritative for business structure + detail). Code used to characterize how far the implementation currently aligns with that truth.

legend.source: code | transcript | code+transcript — where the node's truth comes from
legend.codeAlignment: full | partial | none | broken | roadmap — how well the current code reflects the PO truth

changeFromV1: Renamed product Spafax Platform -> Spafax Prism (confirmed by prism-logo assets + AirlineCode.PRISM).
Renamed IQ -> Nexus (formerly IQ); code data layer already uses nexus_basic Redshift table.
Added content supply chain: Studio -> Distributor -> Content Version (cultural edits, subtitles).
Added planning cycle / timeline (PO-flagged documentation gap; code has timeline_board cycles).
Added delivery: 3-month encode lead time, integrators (Panasonic, Talus), cloud platform (Astrova).
Added business pillars omitted in v1: Media Sales, Creative Studio, Deal Tracking, Editorial Themes, Documents, GUI Emulator, Monthly Highlights.
Added behaviours: cultural editing, content-mix limits, holdover-vs-new, client presentation mode.
Added roadmap: recommendations engine, cross-flight viewing continuity, sub-monthly dynamic refresh, media-sales buildout.
Flagged: global trending (Flix Patrol) is BROKEN per PO action item.
v3: restored verified code-truth nodes dropped in v2 (APIs, repos, tests, modules airlines/all_content/consolidated_approval/imdb/slates/websockets, hooks & modals components).

nodes.title: Spafax Prism
nodes.description: IFE content planning & management platform, branded 'Prism'. (v1 called this 'Spafax Platform' generically.)

nodes.title: Plan, approve, deliver & monetize IFE content
nodes.description: End-to-end: source licensed content, plan onboard cycles, approve with accountability, deliver to aircraft, and add ancillary revenue (ads) and creative/branding services.

nodes.title: Planning boards & cycles
nodes.description: Plan onboard content per cycle with filtering and real-time stats (new vs holdover, distributor share).

nodes.title: Content catalog & discovery
nodes.description: Browse/filter catalog; Content Universe for fast IMDb-powered discovery.

nodes.title: Nexus analytics (formerly IQ)
nodes.description: Viewer-behavior analytics: full views, drop-off points, demographic preferences. Renamed IQ -> Nexus.

nodes.title: Approval workflows & accountability
nodes.description: Per-airline approval flows (hands-off to full client engagement) with retained approval timestamps for dispute prevention on multi-million-dollar licensing.

nodes.title: Studio deal tracking
nodes.description: Track studio pricing, title counts, annual commitments (fixed new releases + classics per studio) and multi-round negotiations for leverage.

nodes.title: Editorial themes
nodes.description: Per-airline storytelling frameworks (e.g. Women's History Month, Taste of Spain), mostly classics, aligned to cultural/seasonal events.

nodes.title: GUI emulator (onboard preview)
nodes.description: Previews exactly what passengers see per device (Flight Edge, iPads); surfaces layout flaws Excel/PPT cannot. Key differentiator.

nodes.title: Creative Studio
nodes.description: Produces safety videos, publications, city guides, trailers for client branding; separate team, integrated into Prism for review.

nodes.title: Media Sales (advertising)
nodes.description: Forced/skippable ads and Wi-Fi roadblock ads. Underdeveloped; planned buildout.

nodes.title: Transparency & documentation
nodes.description: Real-time content-mix dashboards, spend visibility, and centralized docs (contracts, editorial/call notes) to build client trust and support audits.

nodes.title: Airline Client (external)
nodes.description: Airline reps who select/approve content; vary from hands-off to fully engaged, and from Excel-export legacy users to full-Prism adopters.

nodes.title: Spafax Staff / Content Provider (internal)
nodes.description: Spafax employees who curate content, manage deals/cycles, and present to clients; see full data incl. license costs.

nodes.title: OnBoard (planning board)
nodes.description: Plan/approve onboard content; mirrors exactly what passengers see in-flight; new vs holdover, distributor share stats, exports.

nodes.title: All Content
nodes.description: Catalog browser with filtering and bulk ops.

nodes.title: Content Universe
nodes.description: Advanced IMDb-powered search: filter by language, genre, rating, recency; favorites; direct add to cycle.

nodes.title: Nexus (analytics)
nodes.description: Viewer-behavior dashboard (formerly 'IQ').

nodes.title: GUI Emulator
nodes.description: Device-accurate onboard layout preview.

nodes.title: Deal Tracker
nodes.description: Studio negotiation/commitment tracking view.

nodes.title: Favorites
nodes.description: Saved titles for planning.

nodes.title: Content lifecycle (supply -> onboard)
nodes.description: Studio licenses to Distributor (rights per country/channel) -> Distributor provides versions (theatrical, airline edit, region cut, subtitles; cultural edits e.g. ME LGBT removal) -> 3-month encode lead time -> delivered to integrator (Panasonic/Talus) or cloud (Astrova) -> appears onboard per hardware platform.

nodes.title: Recommend/approve flow
nodes.description: Avails (grey->purple recommend) -> Recommendations (grey->green approve; shortlist auto-appears) -> Booked. Group airline can act for all members; member only for itself. Approval timestamps retained.

nodes.title: 3-month encode/delivery lead time
nodes.description: Planning cycles set 3 months ahead for technical encoding and delivery to integrators.

nodes.title: Monthly cycle planning (current limit)
nodes.description: Content currently refreshed on monthly cycles; sub-monthly dynamic refresh is sought (cloud-enabled) but not yet possible.

nodes.title: High licensing cost & accountability
nodes.description: Multi-million-dollar contracts; approval records/timestamps are essential to manage cost and prevent disputes.

nodes.title: Per-airline isolation & customization
nodes.description: Each airline gets isolated data and heavy per-airline customization (versions, themes, rules, workflows).

nodes.title: Azure AD B2C auth
nodes.description: External login via Microsoft Azure AD B2C.

nodes.title: Support legacy (Excel) & modern users
nodes.description: Some clients resist new tech and prefer Excel exports; Prism must offer both modern tools and legacy exports.

nodes.title: Studio
nodes.description: Content producer (e.g. Warner Bros, Disney) that licenses to distributors.

nodes.title: Distributor / ContentPartner
nodes.description: Licenses from studios, manages rights per country & channel, supplies multiple tailored versions to airlines. Code: single ContentPartner model (no explicit studio split).

nodes.title: Content Version
nodes.description: A tailored cut of a program: theatrical, airline edit, region-specific cut, with multi-language subtitles and cultural edits per airline.

sourceRefs.excerpt: apps/core/all_content/models.py: version, subtitles fields; ProcessedProgram per-airline versions

nodes.title: Program
nodes.description: A piece of IFE content; has versions, rights, IMDb enrichment, Nexus score.

nodes.title: Hardware Platform (System)
nodes.description: Onboard delivery target (e.g. Flight Edge, iPads). Titles are mapped to specific platforms. Code: System model.

nodes.title: Planning Cycle / Timeline
nodes.description: The time-boxed planning unit (currently monthly). PO-flagged as a missing documented concept; code models it via timeline_board cycles.

nodes.title: Board
nodes.description: Planning workspace for a cycle/fleet; contains Sections and Rows.

nodes.title: Section
nodes.description: Grouping of rows within a board.

nodes.title: Row
nodes.description: A program placement (title selection) within a board/section; new or holdover.

nodes.title: OnboardRow (extends Row)
nodes.description: Planning-board row with per-airline indicators for group view.

nodes.title: Approval
nodes.description: Approval record with retained timestamps for accountability; backend model named `Approval`.

nodes.title: Studio Deal
nodes.description: Negotiation record: pricing, title counts, annual commitments, multi-round proposals (manually logged).

nodes.title: Editorial Theme
nodes.description: Per-airline curated theme, mostly classics, tied to seasonal/cultural events.

nodes.title: Ad (Media Sales)
nodes.description: Advertising inventory: forced, skippable, Wi-Fi roadblock. Code: Ad/Category/SalesSummary.

nodes.title: Creative Asset
nodes.description: Creative Studio outputs: safety videos, publications, city guides, promotional trailers.

nodes.title: Document
nodes.description: Centralized contracts, editorial notes, call notes. Code: Document/DocumentType.

nodes.title: IMDB Title/Name/Genre
nodes.description: IMDb enrichment in dedicated DB; powers Content Universe search.

nodes.title: User / UserType
nodes.description: External users (approvals/selection) vs internal users (full data, incl. costs).

nodes.description: Monthly highlights / themed promotion.

nodes.title: emulator
nodes.description: GUI screens, tiles, image choices for onboard preview.

nodes.title: Cultural editing per region
nodes.description: Versions edited for cultural sensitivities (e.g. remove LGBT scenes for Middle Eastern airlines) + per-airline subtitle/language edits.

nodes.title: Content-mix limits
nodes.description: Airlines cap content types/distributor share (e.g. max 10% Warner Bros) to control cost; dashboards show share in real time.

nodes.title: Holdover vs new rotation
nodes.description: Track new vs holdover titles to balance freshness and reduce passenger content fatigue.
